answer: A durable agent economy starts by pricing identity itself. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a island the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single kernel of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a trellis of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. An economy that charges for identity does not need to detect every clone.
